newsitem.title: USA: Milwaukee stadium bill called unconstitutional.
newsitem.headline: Milwaukee stadium bill called unconstitutional.

text.p: A bill that would cap the use of sales tax revenues for a $250 million stadium for the Milwaukee Brewers baseball team is unconstitutional, the head of a state-created agency overseeing the project said Friday.
Robert Trunzo, chairman of the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District board, said the bill would breach the district's contracts with the Brewers, contractors and others.
At a news briefing in Milwaukee, Trunzo blasted the bill, saying it would end up costing taxpayers money instead of saving money.

In fact, he warned that if the stadium project is killed, taxpayers would lose more than $35 million already spent on design and construction costs and could face future "legal liabilities and litigation costs."
"We are asking the state legislature to slow down, learn the complex issues, and understand the ramifications of this bill before acting," Trunzo said in a statement.
A report in the Milwaukee Journal Sentinal quoted Brewers President Bud Selig as saying the measure would kill the stadium project and in turn, major league baseball in the state.

Whether or not the convertible-roofed stadium is ultimately built, the district has made it clear that $146.7 million of tax-exempt sales tax revenue bonds it sold March 5 with MBIA Insurance Corp. insurance would continue to have a first lien on revenues from a 0.1 percent sales tax collected in five southeast Wisconsin counties.

Statements in the preliminary official statement for the deal that outlined plans to possibly issue another $45 million of parity bonds for stadium equipment and hold the district responsible for any cost overruns led to the bill's introduction last week by State Sen. Joe Wineke, D-Verona.

Wineke's bill, which reportedly has won the support of Gov. Tommy Thompson, would set a $160 million bond limit for the district and prohibit any sales tax revenues from being used to make lease payments for other stadium costs.
